name: Abusement Park
era: Added in BBR v1.3.2 (iOS notes dated Aug 24, 2012) [Game text via wiki]; skybox fixed in 1.3.4 (Oct 20, 2012) [Game text via wiki]; in BBG from the May 2013 relaunch [Fan-wiki]; FFA mode from BBG 2.5 (Nov 27, 2013) [Game text via wiki]; game-wide 'New Map Lighting' in BBG 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021) [Game text via wiki], after which footage is darker and bluer [Observed]. No map-specific rework documented.
in_2026: Not named in any official text, including the Steam store copy [Canon]. Shown in official media [Observed]: the Steam trailer's red base (about 17.6-22.0 s; 2013 footage [Inference, strong]), the official teaser's 'SAME' panel, and the map tile in the thumbnail of the official Short 'BBG Maps Ranked part 1' (a 16-slot tier list). The 2026 soundtrack opens with 'Abusement Park' (0:54) and adds a 3:05 'Full Version' [Canon]. Fan playtest #3 uploads (Aug 21-23, 2026) list Team Battle/TDM and 'KC' (Kill Confirmed) matches on it [Unverified]; a build '3.0.2' frame shows its EXIT stairs [Observed]. Launch rotation very likely [Inference].
setting: A run-down, horror-tinged night carnival sealed inside tall cracked stone walls, with void beyond [Observed]. 'A horror-themed carnival' [Fan-wiki]; the name is a pun on 'Amusement Park' [Fan-wiki]. Signs read 'ONLY ONE CAN LEAVE', '[NO ENTRY]' and 'CONDEMNED', and the EXIT costs 'Only 400,000 Tix' [Observed]. No stated location.
palette_and_lighting: Dusk-to-night plum sky #231228 with blue-violet clouds #1d1939-#2b1f3b and a maroon horizon glow #3f253b-#473244 (2012-14); near-black plum #100515 in 2021+ and #180519 in the Steam trailer (2013 footage [Inference, strong]). Grey-mauve stone walls #796c72, asphalt #4d4c4c-#625a41. Warm salmon red-base deck #ffa67f with red stencils #fd1a12; cool blue-side deck #ad9777 with blue graffiti #0d4a75. Tents: maroon/white #4c0906-#7c0e0e, orange/yellow #fe9532/#df650c, green #6d8e48, blue/white with white sawtooth trim. Yellow U-rails #ffc32b, red/teal bunting, coaster cars #53bc01 with pink Huggables #db03a9. Baked theatrical lighting with bulb marquees and glowing jump pads (2012); post-2021 and 2026 frames are cooler, with a dark teal floor (#1d3444) and cyan-lit tent stripes [Observed].
landmarks: Perimeter roller coaster on red-white candy-striped pylons, with lime-green cars ridden by grinning pink Huggables. Red base: '[RED]' stencil wall, dripping red stars, salmon plank deck, yellow U-rails. The Mirrored House (mirror-lettered teal marquee, 'LIKE A HOUSE BUT BACKWARDS' sign). The Pump-A-Chump 'FULLA' LEAD' shooting gallery. A big maroon-and-white square tent with three green peaked tents and an octagonal striped gazebo. EXIT stairs under 'Only 400,000 Tix', flanked by twin 'COMING 201…' posters, and a riveted arch daubed 'ONLY ONE CAN LEAVE' [Observed].
hazards_and_easter_eggs: No environmental hazards documented [Unverified]; fully walled, void outside. Jump pads (octagonal, yellow-black ring, cyan glow). Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich in the gazebo/shed near Blue's spawn [Fan-wiki]; in BBR, Bearzerker and Bonus Joules under the bridge [Fan-wiki]. Plant the Bomb bombs sit in front of the House of Mirrors [Fan-wiki]. Easter eggs: Battle Bears Fortress tower art ('Waste Chewer', 'Robowizardhat') [Fan-wiki][Observed]; twin 'COMING 201…' posters (the wiki's '2010's' and/or unreleased-Soldier-skin posters) [Observed][Inference]; three 'MOS DELISH' posters [Observed] (BLAST link unverified); 'Not Wil's CANDY STASH' over a burnt hole; 'Jeepers Peepers! / WHAT'S IN THE BOX?' billboard; 'SLOWBURN II - You're toast.' toaster poster and toaster cutout; 'RED' painted in blue and 'BBR#1' on the Blue side (the wiki says 'BBR FOREVER'); '[RA…E US' stencil with stars; 'Fried Stick on a Stick' / 'ULTRA STICK' on the CONDEMNED crate.

name: Aztec Attack (originally "Facing Temples")
era: Added in BBR v1.3.1, June 28, 2012, as "Facing Temples" [Game text via wiki]. Renamed Aztec Attack at the 2013 BBG relaunch (the BBR wiki page calls it "the v2.0 installment"; the new app's own version list restarts at 1.0, May 24, 2013). The wiki page was moved 2013-06-04 and SkyVu used the aztec-attack URL slug by Aug 2013. FFA arrived in BBG 2.5 (Nov 27, 2013). No map-specific rework is documented; BBG 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021) brought game-wide "New Map Lighting". Servers shut down Mar 12, 2024 [Fan-wiki].
in_2026: Track 13 "Aztec Attack" (1:20) on the official 2026 OST [Canon]. A fan video of SkyVu's Aug 21, 2026 playtest has the chapter "Aztec Attack FFA", and its chapter thumbnail shows the 2026 HUD on this map [Observed]. The Steam-page trailer shows the map, but it re-edits the May 2013 launch trailer, so that footage is from 2013 [Inference, strong]. The store text does not name the map. Launch inclusion is a strong inference. The Oct 2026 "Lighting improvements" may change the look.
setting: Night-time Mesoamerican-style temple arena on a peanut-shaped plateau island in a lava sea. The layout is point-symmetric (180° rotation). Two stepped temples face each other, and each team's base is inside its temple [Fan-wiki]. A central lava pool holds a faceted obsidian rock with 2 cyan pads, crossed sideways by stepping stones that join two ruined pavilions with dark grey roof slabs. 16 mask-face stone cubes and rows of square pillars stand on the sand.
palette_and_lighting: Night sky: indigo zenith #010123–#05032B with stars, then plum #41082F, crimson #7D0E36 and a raspberry horizon #9E1138, over maroon hills #410602. Sand burnt orange #D85C2D (2013 footage; 2012 browner #7B4521). Sandstone #A85936–#CD7D51, with grey carved stone #3E2E28–#473B31 on flat ledges and roofs. Lava sea #FFAC10, pool #FF9D23. Obsidian #280402. Cyan pads #42C7CC. Gems teal #3C715F, rose #ED625B, violet #884956. Red-temple panels #D74925–#EB4220. Lava-thrown warm light, soft shadows; the cool accents are only pads and teal gems. No weather.
landmarks: (1) Twin stepped temples facing each other. (2) Grand front staircase: a lower flight to a dark doorway framed by gem-mosaic panels, then a steep upper flight up a truncated-pyramid top to a square summit. (3) Central lava pool with an obsidian rock and stepping-stone causeway. (4) Lava sea all around the island. (5) Two ruined pavilions with dark grey carved roof slabs and cobblestone plinths. (6) Mask-face stone cubes and free-standing square pillars on cracked sand. One temple's panels glow red, the other's are teal.
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Lava kills and counts as a suicide [Fan-wiki]. Jump pads: the wiki says 12; 14 markers are counted (4 up each temple's back to the summit perch, 4 at the pool corners, 2 on the rock). Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich on the rock, Shields inside the ruins (one seen in an official thumbnail), Health Packs at the temple entrances, Imperial Basket Grande by a block right of each temple [Fan-wiki]. Several Mini Me and stall glitches [Fan-wiki]. Wiki claims Over Clocked Oliver and Astoria symbols at the spawns (added 2013; never seen in any image) [Fan-wiki, Unverified]. The Facing Worlds name nod is fan speculation added in 2025. Flames in one fan thumbnail are a Killdoba glitch.

name: Desert Airmine
era: BBR 1.0 launch map (Oct 8, 2011 per wiki) [Fan-wiki]; removed at the BBG relaunch ('update 2.0', ~May 2013) [Fan-wiki; Inference]; returned in BBG v2.7 (Jan 23, 2014) [Fan-wiki]; drill made 'more erratic' in BBR 1.4.3 [Fan-wiki]; 'New Map Lighting' in BBG 3.0, Nov 2021 [Game text via wiki]
in_2026: In the Aug and Oct 2026 playtest builds. A fan frame from the Oct 15 final playtest (build 3.0.7, FFA) shows it [Observed: i.ytimg.com/vi/1MP1rFi4t-Q/maxres3.jpg; identification Inference]. Fan chapters list Team Battle and FFA matches [Unverified]. OST track 12 'Desert Airmine' 1:13 [Canon]. A sunlit desert tile appears in SkyVu's 16-map collage [Observed]. Not named in the store copy, trailer or screenshots; launch inclusion likely but unstated [Inference].
setting: Sand-topped mesa islands floating in three tiers inside a deep red-rock canyon, built up as an oil 'airmine' with steel lattice towers, cables and girders; 'desert-like surroundings', 'Open-air', 'Day, Sunlight' [Fan-wiki; Observed]. Asymmetrical: Red spawns on the lowest tier, Blue on the big middle tier around a helipad [Fan-wiki].
palette_and_lighting: Powder-to-pale blue sky (#98B4C7 in 2014; #B5D6E1 in 2026); saturated golden-yellow sand (#F1A62F to #FBE31B); terracotta cliffs (#A86038–#C87749, #744531–#84624B in game) over near-black undersides (#1E0D0B); green cacti #114B0A; cyan jump-pad glow #47CBCD [Observed, sampled]. Renders use a low sun on frame-left with aqua haze; in game it is flat, bright daylight; the 2026 frame shows bright daylight with strong bloom on lit sand [Observed].
landmarks: Central drill tower: an octagonal funnel head with a yellow Graham emblem (hard hat, teal goggles, white moustache), slatted paddle arms, and a heavy bit or block over a square shaft [Observed]. Windmill on a lattice tower, the sniper perch [Observed; Fan-wiki]. Round Blue helipad with a red H [Observed overhead; Fan-wiki]. Floating red-cliffed mesas [Observed]. Sombrero cacti [Observed; Fan-wiki 2012–13]. Long wooden plank across the canyon [Fan-wiki; Observed].
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Falling off, hitting the moving drill mid-jump, or touching the windmill rotor all count as suicides [Fan-wiki]. The hole in the Blue base drops to a hidden island with a Bearscream Sandwich and a single jump-pad exit that Engineers mine [Fan-wiki]. Easter eggs: Graham's face on the drill, called 'the first clue' of the Engineer [Fan-wiki]; a blue portable toilet, matching the wiki's 'small toilet and three tool sheds' [Observed; Fan-wiki]; a pumpjack-style walking beam and bear-face barrels [Observed].

name: Frozen Pundra
era: BBG v2.7. The wiki dates it January 23, 2014 (iOS) [Fan-wiki]; the official video is "BATTLE BEARS GOLD Update 2.7 "Frozen Pundra" Map Preview" [Canon]. It was never a BBR map [Inference]. No map-specific rework is recorded; BBG 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021) lists game-wide "New Map Lighting" [Fan-wiki update log].
in_2026: Probably returns, not confirmed. Steam copy does not name it [Canon]. The official 2026 soundtrack has track 10 "Frozen Pundra" (0:54) [Canon]. SkyVu's "Playtest Highlights Part 2" (Aug 26, 2026) has a frame that is almost certainly this map in a team mode [Observed + Inference]. "BBG Maps Ranked part 1" (Oct 11, 2026) puts its tile in the "13-16" row, but that grid is a classic-era collage also used by a fan [Observed]. The final playtest lists "Lighting improvements" [Canon].
setting: A fully enclosed ice cave, snow-covered almost throughout, with an icicle-fringed ice ceiling and no sky [Fan-wiki + Observed]. No story location is documented [Unverified]. The name is likely a 'tundra' pun [Inference]. Do not confuse it with the outdoor 2.6 Christmas loading-screen snowfield [Observed].
palette_and_lighting: Bright, cool, candy-blue cave with flat ambient light, no visible source and no hard shadows [Observed]. Snow is sky-cyan #6FB0F7 to #92E1FB; the ceiling is periwinkle #668FEC; rock is deep indigo #19285A to slate #2E395D; patches are lavender-mauve #866A83 to #B28FB1 [Observed]. The grid tile reads mauve, with plum rock #2D2B3C. The probable 2026 frame is saturated cyan #28B3E1 with deep blue #21358B [Observed]. No falling snow seen.
landmarks: A snow-capped dark faceted rock dome at the centre, with an archway and launch pads at its base. A raised, broad, snow-topped ring track on dark rock supports and arches. An icicle-fringed ceiling with big pale shootable icicles. Hourglass stalactite-stalagmite columns and glassy ice masses. Tall snow mounds. A small snowman outside the track [Fan-wiki + Observed].
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Large lightly coloured icicles fall when shot: they take several seconds to drop, do little damage over a small area, and disappear on hitting the floor [Fan-wiki]. A jump pad under the dome leads to the Bearscream Sandwich near the dome roof (double damage for 20 s; respawns every 90 s) [Fan-wiki]. The cramped layout snags Turkish SW Boots users [Fan-wiki]. The easter egg is a small snowman outside the track [Fan-wiki]; a tiny white eared figure in the grid tile is probably it [Observed/Inference].

name: Gold Digger
era: BBG launch, May–June 2013: one of the 2013 trailer's '3 New Maps' with Skate or Die and Sky View [Canon]. The wiki's '2.0' means this launch [Fan-wiki]. Not a BBR map [Inference]. Pickup layout changed across wiki edits from 2013 to 2026 [Fan-wiki]. 2.6.1 (Jan 4, 2014) fixed a class spawning with the Bearscream Sandwich here [Game text via wiki]. Game-wide 'New Map Lighting' in 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021) [Game text via wiki]. Servers shut down March 12, 2024 [Fan-wiki]
in_2026: Named on Steam as a returning 'Iconic Map' [Canon]. OST track 4 'Gold Digger' (0:38) [Canon]. One of 16 map stills in SkyVu's 'BBG Maps Ranked part 1' thumbnail (Oct 11, 2026) [Observed]. A fan video of the Oct 15, 2026 final playtest lists it as a Team Battle match [Unverified: fan source], and its storyboard frames show the map in the 2026 build: same sky, walls, carts and gems, slightly brighter and greyer [Observed]. FFA and PTB support unconfirmed
setting: A night-time open-pit gold mine: an oval pit open to a navy starry sky (full moon in the 2013 trailer), walled by tiers of stacked rock blocks, with timber-roofed rail tunnels off it [Observed]. The wiki calls it 'a mining cave' [Fan-wiki]. Out of bounds you see Sky View's city, and the two maps share a skybox [Fan-wiki]
palette_and_lighting: Low-key night. Warm charcoal-plum rock walls #170E0F (highlight #302525). Boulders #393032. Ochre floor #3F2A13. Olive-brown shaft walls #181008 into black #000000. Timber #331D02. Gold load #DDA612 to #FFD50E. Blue gem #0206E7, red gem #591614 to #921408. Jump-pad cyan #31BFE1. Navy sky #00172B with moon #ACC6D8. Warm glows from gold, lamps and floor light pools; cool tones only in the sky and moon; the rock stays warm and dark to its crest [Observed]. 2026 frames are a bit brighter and greyer (sky #0E2B40) [Observed, low-res]
landmarks: Twin black shafts on a diagonal, split by a narrow stone-edged floor-level 'bridge' with the Bearscream Sandwich at its middle. Bowl of stacked-rock walls under stars and a moon. Glowing gold carts on opposite stone ledges. Straight rail tunnel with timber frames and octagonal hanging lamps (the map icon). Fenced rail openings and timber mouths marked by red or blue faceted gems. Cyan jump pads with hazard-striped rims
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Falling into the shafts kills you, and a Shield won't save you [Fan-wiki]. Two jump pads [Observed]. Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich on the bridge, Shields and Imperial Basket Grandes outside the spawns (the IBG is probably the floating pickup on a raised ledge), Health Packs inside them [Fan-wiki; Inference]. Sky View city visible out of bounds and a shared skybox [Fan-wiki]. 'Red team advantage' IBG trivia, contradicted by wiki history [Fan-wiki]. 2.6.1 Bearscream spawn bug, Arbiter vs Assault unresolved [Game text via wiki]

name: H.I.P. Test Lab (originally Huggable Factory)
era: BBR 1.0 launch map, 2011 (wiki: Oct 8, 2011), under the name 'Huggable Factory'. Renamed H.I.P. Test Lab with the BBG relaunch (wiki: BBG 1.0 May 24, 2013; page moved Jun 4, 2013); exact build unverified. Modes: team mode from launch, Plant the Bomb from BBR 1.3 (May 3, 2012), FFA from BBG 2.5 (Nov 27, 2013). The So Fly exploit to its secret rooms was fixed in BBR 1.4.2 (Feb 28, 2013) per the wiki. No rework or removal is documented.
in_2026: Included in practice. The SkyVu 2026 soundtrack lists 'Huggable Factory' (0:54) and the Full Version (2:52) [Canon]. The Steam trailer shows it at about 34.3-36.8 s, and Steam screenshot ss_487a600c is the same walkway shot [Observed]. Both are most likely 2013 footage SkyVu re-used [Inference, strong]; the 3.0.7 fan frames are the 2026 evidence. The official 'BBG Maps Ranked part 1' short (Oct 11, 2026) shows its tube-room art among 16 map images [Observed]. Fan uploads of the Oct 15 final playtest show it in build 3.0.7_2026.11.19_b7 [Observed]. The Steam text does not name it. The displayed 2026 name and the effect of the official 'Lighting improvements' are unverified.
setting: An indoor H.I.P. Huggable lab and factory with no windows or sky. Pink Huggables float in glowing tubes. Overhead rails carry hanging pink Huggable dolls, and lofts hold crates stamped with a Huggable face. Per the wiki: 'a big metallic stage', two levels, point-symmetric bases, and an inaccessible loading bay where a Pelican't is loaded 'against the backdrop of a large ship in space'. The exact location is undocumented.
palette_and_lighting: High-key, almost shadowless white interior. Lab white #B5ABAA-#D3CCCC, walkway #BBB3B5-#D3CCCC, magenta lofts #1D0016-#5C014B up to #FF01E4, crate charcoal #080707, Huggable/doll pink #D81C73-#F12680, team blue #0023F0 (door glow #245BD6), jump-pad cyan #3CC2CB with hazard yellow #DABA26, and a diagonal rainbow-striped column. Tube room: translucent pink diamond-light wall #D17BA6-#F3A6CD (2026: #F58FE8), cyan tube rings #31B2ED, cyan-lit floor #B2E1FB, grey-blue ceiling #7B8AA5. Secret room: taupe walls #756053 with an amber floor pool #FCDD69.
landmarks: 1) A Huggable tube room in each base: five glowing glass tubes with floating pink Huggables in front of a translucent pink wall of diamond lights. 2) Twin octagonal towers and the centre bridge (Bearscream Sandwich) over a 35-crate floor. 3) The production line: rails of hanging pink dolls, a grey robotic claw, a rainbow-striped column with a black funnel, magenta crate lofts. 4) Team-coloured portal doors and white pillars with two big blue up-triangles over a jump pad. 5) Hidden rooms where about 20 Huggables watch a static-filled monitor of a red-visored figure (wiki: Rho). 6) An inaccessible loading bay with a Pelican't, probably the hanging-crate bay over a yellow area seen in 2012 footage.
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Jump pads (BBR-era wiki: only two; one is visible beside the blue-arrow pillar in 2026). Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich on the centre bridge, two Imperial Basket Grande on the centre crates, two Health Packs in the far corners by the crates near the inclines, Shields in the tube rooms; Bonus Joules under the bridges in the BBR era. PTB: both bombs under the main bridge; bomb tubes behind the Huggable tubes. Kill floor in the loading bay. Easter eggs: the Huggable 'training' rooms behind a 'purple-pink force field' (So Fly access fixed in BBR 1.4.2; per the wiki still reachable with Mini Me plus Turkish SW Boots), and a hidden Pelican't. The wiki says H.I.P. parodies Evangelion's Human Instrumentality Project. All are Fan-wiki except the visuals marked Observed.

name: Haunted Castle
era: BBR v1.3.3 Halloween update, dated Oct 10, 2012 by the wiki [Game text via wiki]. Removed in the wiki's '2.0', best read as the BBG relaunch of May 24, 2013 [Fan-wiki; Inference]. Returned in BBG 2.4 on Oct 24, 2013: 'To celebrate the holiday, the Haunted Castle map has made a return!' [Canon]. Fan titles place it in play at Halloween 2015 and Oct-Nov 2021 [Unverified]. Servers shut down Mar 12, 2024 [Fan-wiki].
in_2026: Not named on the Steam store [Canon, by absence]. Its track 'Haunted Castle' (1:01, track 11) is on the official BBG soundtrack, out Nov 4, 2026 [Canon]. Fan metadata places it in the playtests: InstableGR's Jul 29, 2026 PC Playtest #2, 'Match 8 (Kill Confirmed, Haunted Castle, Tillman/B-1000)', and droid BBG's Sep 25, 2026 'Haunted Castle FFA', whose build stamp appears to read 2026 [Unverified]. Launch rotation, and whether it is seasonal, is unconfirmed.
setting: A Halloween castle at night on a figure-8 floating island over black void: a square slate-blue curtain-walled castle with a tall central tower on four legs, and graveyard lawns where each team spawns. Underground tunnels link the bases to the courtyard [Observed; Fan-wiki for the tunnels]. Do not confuse it with the daytime 2018 Battle Royale castle ('Castle Royale') [Observed; Inference].
palette_and_lighting: Night. Black to violet starry sky (#000000-#160015) with a faint magenta horizon glow over dark hills. A large grey jack-o'-lantern-faced moon (#AFB0B0) appears in 2013 gameplay. Cool slate walls (#1B3541-#2A2D43). Terracotta courtyard (#BA513F lit, #3D272E shadow) with a warm sand-gold pool under the tower (#D3974F). Jack-o'-lanterns on plank brackets glow #D64D08 to #FF9208; there are no flame torches. Green window glow #315539. Lawns #162619-#325013, hedges #2A2C00. Graveyard stones violet #5A54B0 or warm beige #B78262. Banners red #640302-#730810 and blue #0A01C9. Pumpkins #D06000, crates #733C1F, iron #1D2123. The pink moon and magenta wash are promo grading [Observed; Inference].
landmarks: The central stilted tower with plank walkways, a lit opening and pads beneath it, and a green window. The team gatehouses: black spiked portcullis between red or blue bear-emblem banners, jack-o'-lanterns on brackets, gate switch above. The memorial name slab beside a scalloped R.I.P. stone and the iron railing in each spawn graveyard. The jack-o'-lantern moon. The terracotta courtyard with crate-and-pumpkin piles beside octagonal pits. Graveyard lawns with rounded headstones over earth plots, tall hedges and a cave-like tunnel entrance.
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Melee-toggled switches (one above each team gate) open and close gates in the underground passages [Fan-wiki]. Jump pads under the central tower. Two Bearscream Sandwiches at opposite ends; 2 Grandes, 2 Health Packs and Shields. A hidden outer ledge leads to a jagged hole into the courtyard (needs SW Boots or Jump). Falling into the void kills [Fan-wiki]. Gravestone names: MK, Lt. Action, Rob, Trang, An, Jackson, Grimes, 1nachoboy5 and Apothecy, in three columns [Observed; Fan-wiki]; show only Jackson and Grimes legibly.

name: Marecraft (Marecraft Arena / "The Marecraft")
era: Added in BBR ("Battle Bears") update 1.4.3, released as 1.4.3.1: Apr 15 and Apr 23, 2013 [Fan-wiki]; teased Apr 5, 2013 [Canon]. In BBG from 1.0 (May 24, 2013) through 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021, "New Map Lighting") [Fan-wiki]. At launch it ran Team Battle and Plant the Bomb; later FFA (v2.5) and King of the Windmill (v2.8–2.29) [Fan-wiki]. No removal or rework is documented.
in_2026: Not named in the Steam store text [Canon]. The official soundtrack has track 8 "Marecraft" 0:57 [Canon]. It is in the 16-tile grid of the official Short "BBG Maps Ranked part 1" (about Oct 12, 2026), which ranks 16 slots [Observed]. Fan playtest chapters list "Marecraft TDM" (Playtest #3) and "Plant the Bomb, Marecraft" (Final PC Playtest, Oct 15, 2026) [Unverified], and a playtest thumbnail shows the map with HUD build 3.0.2 [Observed]. The Steam trailer shot (38.3–41.5 s) is 2013 footage [Inference, strong]. Very likely in the launch roster [Inference, strong].
setting: Inside the digestive system of the Marecraft Carrier, the giant blue-maned unicorn carrying an aircraft carrier that is a boss in Battle Bears: Zombies [Fan-wiki][Observed]. Dark-metal forts, probably Huggable-built [Inference], sit over living flesh, lime-green digestive pools and intestine tunnels [Observed][Fan-wiki]. Layout: a long rectangle with 180° symmetry; red spawn at one end, purple/blue at the other; a central bridge along the team axis, a lower cross-walkway, four pools, metal flank decks, a sniper tower per base and underground tube rooms with jump pads [Observed][Fan-wiki].
palette_and_lighting: Flesh #D23D1F–#E65947 (2013 renders), trailer grade #FF4E28/#F35013; crimson organs #BD3E41/#C2332E; pale apricot ribs and column #EAA758–#FFBC60; pink veins #D87B6F; dark gunmetal deck #794B45 (shaded #4F312B, caps #261D13); navy ring frame #394A64; lime pools #3C7C21 with #4FB13A vein lines; woven fibre #D67649; jump-pad core #69A89C [Observed]. Enclosed warm orange interior, fairly even light, no sky or daylight; chunky low-poly look [Observed].
landmarks: Post-lined dark bridge with A-frame end arches and red/blue sockets over glowing green pools; twin squat sniper towers with satellite dishes and jump pads among their legs; a ring-segmented cream-gold throat column and pale rib vault overhead, with dangling orange lobes; octagonal ring portals (red-faced and navy) into intestine tunnels; gland-nub rows, crimson organ mounds, woven fibre mounds and a unicorn pictogram plaque [Observed][Fan-wiki; identifications Inference].
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Falling into a pool is death, counted as a suicide [Fan-wiki]; gland ledges offer an escape route [Fan-wiki]. Jump pads in the tube rooms [Fan-wiki] and at the tower feet [Observed]. Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich on the bridge, Imperial Basket Grande and 2 Shields at the intersection below, 2 Health Packs on the towers [Fan-wiki]. Easter egg: outlines of the then-unreleased Assassin under the bridge, called the first intentional class leak on the Assassin (BBG) page [Fan-wiki]. Gag: "two separate uvula" [Fan-wiki]. Mini Me ring glitch [Fan-wiki].

name: No Bear's Land (originally "Battlefield Airpad")
era: BBR 1.0 launch map, Oct 8, 2011, as 'Battlefield Airpad' [Fan-wiki]. The official BBR trailer (Nov 23, 2011) thumbnail is set in its trench [Canon/Observed]. Renamed at the 2013 BBG relaunch (wiki 'version 2.0'; BBG, launched May 24, 2013, was a separate app that replaced BBR, per the wiki) [Fan-wiki]. Reskins: winter 2.26 (Jan 17, 2017; 'Winter Map is back' in 2.28, Dec 20, 2017), summer 2.27 (May 29, 2017), spring 2.51 (Apr 13, 2018) [Fan-wiki, Updates]. BBG 3.0 'New Map Lighting' (Nov 15, 2021) applied game-wide [Fan-wiki]. Historic modes: Team Battle, Plant the Bomb (from BBR 1.3), Free-For-All (from 2.5) [Fan-wiki; Observed].
in_2026: Returning [Canon]: the Steam copy says 'jump back into classics such as No Bears Land…', and it is OST track 2 'No Bears Land' (0:44). Seen in three official SkyVu uploads: the Playtest Highlights thumbnail (keep roof, Red 10–Blue 10, build 3.0.0), 'BBG Maps Ranked part 1' (first tile of the 16-map grid), and 'The Most ICONIC Weapon…' maxres1 (Blue keep view) [Observed]. Fan chapter lists put it in Team Battle in the Jul 29, Aug 21 and Oct 15 playtests and in a test mode 'Kill Confirmed' (Jul 29) [Unverified: fan]. Red keep at the north, Blue at the south: octagonal olive concrete towers with cobbled roofs, joined to battlements with boxy grey turrets, and a jump pad at the back. A zig-zag of plank-floored trenches (cartoon soil-strata walls, wooden posts, grey slatted decks with yellow stripes) runs to a centre pillar holding the Bearscream Sandwich between two jump pads. Two crashed Pelican'ts on hills (red-banded west, blue-banded east) trail long dirt furrows and carry super jump pads. A food stand sits beside each keep [Observed; Fan-wiki].

Saturated blue sky (#2F6BC9–#3B72D4 → #7797EA–#8EA7EE in BBR; #819AE5 in 2026) with big white cumulus (#F5F5F8) and misty blue-grey wooded hills. Yellow rim stripe #FBF617. Winter: snow #FEFEFE, ice-cyan sandbags and trench floors (~#80D2CC), sky #A6B7E5. Summer: sand #ECF18E–#FEF787, water #42AEBD, orange umbrellas #D55C25–#E97032, blue bridges #266DAF–#306DA6 [Observed, approximate].
landmarks: 1) Red and Blue keeps: octagonal, team double bands, recessed slab doorway with bullet-cracked pilasters, stencil 'XEL-PMOC 20-11', cobbled roof with a ring pad, battlement with a boxy grey turret. 2) The trench zig-zag: plank floors, striped soil walls with a drooping grass cap, wooden posts, grey yellow-striped decks, sandbag arcs. 3) Two crashed four-engine Pelican'ts on hills, with ploughed furrows, barrels, a snapped-off pod each, and a health pack and super jump pad on top. 4) Centre pillar with the Bearscream Sandwich and twin jump pads. 5) Food stands: red-and-yellow parasol with a drumstick-mascot roundel over a grey cart, with the Imperial Basket Grande glowing beside it. 6) Black X tank traps, daisies, a yellow-striped rim, and fin-shaped corner pylons with team lights [Observed; Fan-wiki].
hazards_and_easter_eggs: Jump pads behind each keep (to the roof), beside the centre pillar, and on each Pelican't ('at a extremely high altitude' to land by the opposite wreck) [Fan-wiki]. Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich ×1 (double damage 20 s, 90 s respawn), Imperial Basket Grande ×2 behind the food stands, Health Pack ×2 on the wrecks, Shield ×2 on the keep roofs [Fan-wiki; top-down markers Observed]. PTB: bomb tubes on the keep roofs, bombs in the centre trenches [Fan-wiki]. 'Suicide: Yes' most likely means falling off the plateau edge [Inference]. Long sightlines favour Sniper and Demo [Fan-wiki]. Easter eggs: the No Man's Land pun; the Pelican't as a Halo Pelican pun with a design based on Aliens' UD-4 Cheyenne [Fan-wiki]; the 'War. What is it good for?' blurb [Canon per notes, Unverified]; a white cartoon bone in the trench soil in the 2012 renders [Observed]; the drumstick mascot beside the fried-food pickup [Observed/Inference]; a winter Christmas tree with a gold star on the pillar [Fan-wiki; Observed]. Ambient: a dark hovering craft with green-glowing pods in the sky (2013 and 2026), identity unknown [Observed].

name: Shortest Parsec
era: Teased in BBR iOS 1.4.1 notes (Jan 10, 2013): "New Space Station map!" [Game text via wiki]. Added in Battle Bears (BBR line) iOS 1.4.2 on Feb 28, 2013, the update that renamed the game to plain "Battle Bears" [Game text via wiki; Fan-wiki]. in_2026: Track 9 "Shortest Parsec" (1:13) on the 2026 soundtrack [Canon]. Launch inclusion likely but unconfirmed [Inference].
setting: A small space station with almost no walls, floating in a starfield [Game text via wiki; Fan-wiki]. Per SkyVu's blurb, a "private arms dealer" uses it "to transfer power to its facilities" on "a mysterious planet on the fringes of the known galaxy", where "a robotic someone" exploded nearby [Canon per notes; Unverified this session]. H.I.P. (Vitruvian-Huggable) emblems on the floor and walls [Fan-wiki; Observed]. Tagline: "In space, EVERYONE can hear you scream."

Lavender-white hulls #8472C7–#98A6F1. Glossy red tower panels #E30315–#FF1B28 with mint-white light bars. Orange-gold beam cone #FEDA68 onto a pad with rim #FF672D and a white core, from a pale sky-blue hex emitter #7EACF7. Hall: red ceiling beams #BF0108, mauve-beige walls #976562, slate floor #131B26, side doors glowing red #FF384A and purple #B24EFF. Teal asteroids #014E61 (Steam trailer, 2013 footage [Inference, strong]) / #526464 (Jan 2013 preview), cyan jump pads #4ED9D8, green console #1F8D64, purple-lit lower level #433777. landmarks: 1) Red-panelled laser tower whose periodic orange cone hits a round pad, holding a Bearscream Sandwich, between the two spawns. 2) White central module ('middle dome') with a red-beamed hall, an open roof slot and red-lit and purple-lit side doors. 3) Spine walkway with a large red H.I.P. floor medallion. 4) Far switch tower ('meteor tower'): cracked red floor, lime-green console, black cable, outline H.I.P. engraving with a skewered pink Huggable. 5) Faceted teal asteroids with hexagonal holes. 6) L-shaped red and blue team arms with dashed running lights; red on the left when facing the laser tower from the far end [Observed].

Jump-pad stall bug [Fan-wiki]. Plant the Bomb bombs sit on the bottom platform under the far tower [Fan-wiki]. name: Tutorial
era: BBR single-player training mode. Its TUTORIAL mode card is on SkyVu's official BBR Sneak Peek menu (Aug 31, 2011, before BBR 1.0 on Oct 8, 2011) [Observed; Canon video]. The arena is first seen in a fan video (Apr 18, 2012) and in a wiki screenshot (Jul 21, 2012). Carried into BBG at launch (BBG 1.0 May 24, 2013) [Fan-wiki]. 2013–14 changes: HUD briefing removed, signs moved, Tutorial-only 7 s Boots recharge dropped, Pro-Mode Jump in the kit, two out-of-bounds exploits patched [Fan-wiki]. Same look in fan captures from 2014, 2015 and 2025 (build 2.53.6). It is a game mode, not a PvP map.
in_2026: Playable in 2026 builds per fan uploads (thumbnails Observed, videos not watched): Jul 9, 2026 (first Windows-only Discord playtest day): 'BBG Tutorial Speedrun (1:20)' by JustNubz and 'Battle Bears gold Tutorial test on pc' by Slinkster, both showing build 2.54.0. Sep 20, 2026 (4th playtest day): Mika_do, touch HUD with a build string reading about '3.0.5_2026…'. SkyVu soundtrack track 18 'Tutorial' 0:32 [Canon]. Not mentioned on the Steam store or in any 2026 news post. Probably not one of the '16 wacky maps' [Inference]. Launch-build status unconfirmed.
setting: A 'virtual' training course [Fan-wiki]: an endless black void of vertical green Latin-letter code rain (Lorem-ipsum 'CONSECTETUR ADIPISC…' legible; Matrix-like, homage is Inference). Dark circuit-grid floor, zig-zag neon arrow walkways at several heights, floating circuit-etched blocks, amber instruction signs on bracket posts, lattice bear dummies and red laser gates [Observed]. The goal is a line-lit hologram of the Pelican't drop ship [Observed; Fan-wiki]. Linear, enclosed by invisible air barriers, single-player, offline, no Gas, 0% damage intake [Fan-wiki]. Fixed kit: Oliver skin, A Salt Rifle 70/70, Bearzooka 1/1, B.E.A.R. Club, Turkish SW Boots, Pro-Mode Jump [Fan-wiki; Observed HUD].
palette_and_lighting: All light is emissive neon with bloom; no sky, sun, shadow, weather or time of day [Observed]. Void #000100 to #000501. Floor #011400 with grid up to #083109. Rain #1C5D23, brightest #3FDE44, a few pale grey glyphs. Walkways #2DC115 to #3EFB22 (2026 up to #53FF37). Floating blocks #00CC00 to #31FD20. Pelican't hologram body #00D201, edges #13F610. Amber signs: interior #4A2C00, rim #F7DB21. Label text #E7E74A to #FFFF76. Bear-head targets #EEFF18. Orange lattice dummies #C4672E to #FF9122. Red dummies #FA0900. Laser bars #D44B14 to #E70507. PICKUPS panels: face #023400, frame #24ED0B. Jump pads: cyan #41D7E8 to #5EE0D4 with hazard yellow #FBD103 [Observed samples, approximate].
landmarks: Hologram Pelican't (four engine pods, two round nose lamps) inside concentric broken green rings, visible from the start. Green digital-rain void. Amber signs on bracket-shaped neon posts (MOVE with a crosshair-and-arrow pictogram; SHOOTING 'DOUBLE TAP SCREEN -OR- TAP FIRE BUTTON'; WEAPON SWITCH / MELEE ATTACK; PICKUPS; TEAM BLUE; JUMP PADS), plus floating 3D labels (MOVING, SHOOTING, MELEE/ WEAPON SWITCH, PICKUPS, USE SPECIAL ITEM, TEAM COLORS, OPTIONS, JUMP PADS) with yellow leader lines. Neon arrow walkways and floating circuit blocks. A PICKUPS row of green-framed dark panels. Orange, red and blue lattice bear dummies. Finish row of standard BBG jump pads (octagonal, hazard-striped rim, cyan star centre, cyan ripple rings) [Observed].
hazards_and_easter_eggs: No damage (0% intake). Laser walls, seen as stacked horizontal red beams, block progress until tasks such as 'shooting the moving targets' are done [Fan-wiki; Observed]. BBR prompt 'JUMP ONTO PLATFORM USING SPECIAL ITEM TO PROCEED' [Observed]. A Bearscream Sandwich that does not respawn (seen in 2026; 'POWER UP' HUD tag plus purple aura) [Fan-wiki; Observed]. Jump pads. Exploits: BBR endless fall past the air barriers, BBG laser-wall launch (both patched), and a still-possible vault off the end line of jump pads [Fan-wiki; fan videos 2012–13]. Secret achievement: wiki called it 'Hey, stop trying to break our game!'; a Jun 2013 fan-video thumbnail shows 'Stop trying to break our…' / 'Hey, stop trying to break our game man…', 10 pts [Observed, low-res; exact title Unverified]. Matrix quotes in BBG text [Game text via wiki]. Lorem ipsum in the rain [Observed]. Tutorial A Salt Rifle has 70 rounds and pre-v1.0 stats [Fan-wiki]. BBR card shows a baby Huggable with a four-pod toy ship [Observed; Fan-wiki].
